name: berth-plugin-docker
description: Creates a long-running Ubuntu container with systemd and SSH, to be set up like any other machine, and runs Compose projects as deployments.

provisioners.label: Docker container
provisioners.description: An Ubuntu 26.04 container with systemd and an SSH server, on the local Docker or on the engine named by host. berth applies its role to it over SSH. It also runs Compose projects there as deployments.

arguments.name: host
arguments.label: Docker endpoint
arguments.help: The Docker engine to use, such as ssh://ops@192.0.2.10. Empty uses the local default.

arguments.name: image
arguments.label: Image
arguments.help: The image to start from. Empty builds the one that comes with the plugin.

arguments.name: runtime
arguments.label: Runtime
arguments.help: privileged runs the container with --privileged, so root in it is root on the Docker host. sysbox runs it with the Sysbox runtime instead, which needs Sysbox on the Docker host.

arguments.name: ssh_port
arguments.label: SSH port
arguments.help: A port of the Docker host to publish the container's SSH on, such as 2222. Empty publishes none.

arguments.name: publish_address
arguments.label: Publish address
arguments.help: The address berth reaches the published SSH port at. A loopback address such as 127.0.0.1 keeps the port on the Docker host's loopback; any other publishes it on every address of the Docker host.

arguments.name: volume
arguments.label: Volume
arguments.help: The volume for /srv/agent, the agent's work. Empty uses berth-HOST-data.

arguments.name: cpus
arguments.label: CPUs
arguments.help: How many CPUs the container may use, such as 4. Empty sets no limit.

arguments.name: memory
arguments.label: Memory
arguments.help: How much memory the container may use, such as 8g. Empty sets no limit.

arguments.name: keep_volume
arguments.label: Keep volume on destroy
arguments.help: Whether deleting the machine keeps its volume, so a new machine can take the agent's work over.

arguments.name: keep_volumes
arguments.label: Keep volumes on remove
arguments.help: Whether removing the deployment keeps the named volumes of its project. no removes them with what is in them.

actions.name: services
actions.label: Services
actions.help: Each container of the project, with its service and its state.

actions.name: restart
actions.label: Restart
actions.confirm: Restart every container of this deployment?
actions.help: Restart the project's containers as they are, without reading the Compose file again.

actions.name: pull
actions.label: Pull and update
actions.confirm: Pull the images of this deployment and recreate the containers whose image changed?
actions.help: Pull the images the Compose file names, then bring the project up again, so containers whose image changed are recreated.

arguments.name: image
arguments.label: Image
arguments.help: The image to start from, such as debian:12 or any image reference. It becomes no berth host: nothing of berth is put in it.

arguments.name: command
arguments.label: Command
arguments.help: The command to run in the container, such as sleep infinity. Empty runs the image's own command.

arguments.name: environment
arguments.label: Environment
arguments.help: Variables for the container, one NAME=VALUE a line. A line starting with # is a comment.

arguments.name: ports
arguments.label: Ports
arguments.help: Ports to publish, comma-separated, such as 8080:80. Empty publishes none.

arguments.name: volumes
arguments.label: Volumes
arguments.help: Volumes to mount, comma-separated, as NAME:/path or /host/path:/path. Bind mounts need absolute paths on the Docker host.

arguments.name: network
arguments.label: Network
arguments.help: The network to attach to. Empty uses the engine's default network.

arguments.name: restart
arguments.label: Restart
arguments.help: Whether the container starts again when the engine or the machine restarts.

arguments.name: cpus
arguments.label: CPUs
arguments.help: How many CPUs the container may use, such as 2. Empty sets no limit.

arguments.name: memory
arguments.label: Memory
arguments.help: How much memory the container may use, such as 2g. Empty sets no limit.

actions.name: engine
actions.label: Check the engine
actions.help: Ask the Docker engine for its version, its runtimes and how many containers berth made there.

actions.name: images
actions.label: Images
actions.help: The images the engine has, with their sizes.

actions.name: volumes
actions.label: Volumes
actions.help: Every volume of the engine, marked when berth made it, and whether a container uses each. One kept with keep_volume stays here until it is removed.

actions.name: create-volume
actions.label: New volume
actions.help: Create a named volume on the engine, which a container can mount.

arguments.name: name
arguments.label: Name
arguments.help: The name of the volume, such as wiki-data.

actions.name: remove-volume
actions.label: Remove volume
actions.confirm: Remove this volume and everything in it?
actions.help: Remove a named volume and what is in it. Docker refuses it while a container uses it.

arguments.name: name
arguments.label: Name
arguments.help: The name of the volume to remove.

actions.name: pull-image
actions.label: Pull image
actions.help: Fetch an image from its registry onto the engine.

arguments.name: image
arguments.label: Image
arguments.help: The image to pull, such as debian:12.

actions.name: remove-image
actions.label: Remove image
actions.confirm: Remove this image from the engine?
actions.help: Remove an image from the engine. Docker refuses it while a container uses it.

arguments.name: image
arguments.label: Image
arguments.help: The image to remove, such as debian:12.

actions.name: build
actions.label: Build the image
actions.help: Build the image the plugin brings, which a new machine starts from unless it names another. Creating the first machine builds it too; this does it ahead of time.

actions.name: prune
actions.label: Remove what berth left behind
actions.confirm: Remove the images of older versions of this plugin that no container uses, and with volumes=yes the volumes berth made that no container uses?
actions.help: Remove the images of older versions of this plugin that no container uses. With volumes=yes also the volumes berth made that no container uses, such as those kept with keep_volume, and the agent's work in them. Nothing berth did not make is touched, and no container is.

arguments.name: volumes
arguments.label: Also volumes
arguments.help: yes also removes the volumes berth made that no container uses, with what is in them.
